did_you_know.text: The prophecy was given in the fourth year of Darius’s reign, on the fourth day of the ninth month, the month of Kislev.
The people of Bethel sent Sharezer, Regem-Melech, and others to seek the favor of the LORD.
The question put to the priests and prophets was whether they should continue mourning and fasting in the fifth month, as they had done for many years.
The LORD reminds them that the fasting and mourning in the fifth and seventh months had continued for seventy years, and asks whether they had really been fasting for him.
The prophet emphasizes that even in eating and drinking, people act first and foremost for themselves; therefore, fasting alone is not the main issue.
Zechariah directs the people to the words of the earlier prophets, spoken when Jerusalem and the surrounding cities were inhabited and peaceful.
The central requirement is to administer true justice and show kindness and compassion to one another.
The LORD commands them not to oppress the widow, the orphan, the foreigner, or the poor, and not to plot evil against one another.
The people are described as refusing to listen, turning a stubborn shoulder, and making their ears too hard to hear.
This expresses the principle of measure for measure: when they called out to the LORD and he did not listen, then when he called to them, they would not listen either.
